name: Kuwait
genZNote: Kuwait's National Assembly is the oldest elected parliament in the Gulf Arab states — proof that even in a region known for absolute monarchies, Kuwait carved out its own distinctly more participatory political tradition decades ago.

sections.heading: 🗺️ Geography
bullets: A small country at the northern tip of the Persian Gulf, bordered by Iraq and Saudi Arabia.
Almost entirely flat desert terrain with very limited arable land and fresh water, relying heavily on desalination.
Kuwait City, the capital, sits on a natural deep-water harbour that has long made it a significant trading port.

sections.heading: 🗣️ People & Culture
bullets: Arabic is the official language; Islam is the state religion, and traditional Gulf Arab and Bedouin customs remain influential.
A large expatriate population, including a significant South Asian and Indian community, forms the majority of Kuwait's overall population.
Historic pearl-diving and seafaring traditions, along with a strong contemporary literary and press culture relative to regional neighbours.

sections.heading: 🏛️ Government & Society
bullets: A constitutional emirate with the Al Sabah family as the ruling dynasty; the Emir is head of state, and Kuwait has the Gulf region's oldest directly elected National Assembly (parliament).
Known for a relatively more open political and press environment compared to some neighbouring Gulf monarchies, though the Emir retains significant powers.
Was invaded and occupied by Iraq in 1990, leading to the Gulf War and a US-led international coalition that restored Kuwaiti sovereignty in 1991.

sections.heading: 🌐 Global Relations
bullets: A founding member of OPEC and a significant oil exporter, though smaller in scale than Saudi Arabia or the UAE.
Maintains close security ties with the United States following the 1990-91 Gulf War, and plays an active mediating role in regional Gulf diplomacy.
Member of the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) and Arab League.

sections.heading: 🇮🇳 Relations with India
bullets: India and Kuwait share long-standing relations, with Kuwait being an important source of crude oil imports for India and a significant destination for Indian expatriate workers.
Kuwait's currency, the Kuwaiti Dinar, is among the highest-valued currencies in the world, making remittances from Indian workers economically significant.
Cooperation has grown in defence, investment, and labour welfare, with periodic high-level visits strengthening ties.

sections.heading: 📦 Trade & Economy
bullets: An oil-dependent economy, with petroleum exports historically accounting for the majority of government revenue.
Kuwait Investment Authority is one of the world's oldest and largest sovereign wealth funds, diversifying oil wealth into global investments.
Efforts underway to diversify the economy, including growing trade, logistics, and financial services sectors.

sections.heading: ⭐ What It's Known For
bullets: Having the Gulf region's oldest elected National Assembly.
The 1990-91 Gulf War, following Iraq's invasion and subsequent liberation of Kuwait.
One of the world's oldest and largest sovereign wealth funds (Kuwait Investment Authority).
The Kuwaiti Dinar being among the world's highest-valued currencies.

sections.heading: 💰 Currency & Economy
bullets: Currency: Kuwaiti Dinar (KWD), among the highest-valued currencies in the world.
Economy is overwhelmingly oil-dependent, with some of the world's largest proven oil reserves.
Maintains one of the largest sovereign wealth funds globally.

sections.heading: 🌿 Ecology & Environment
bullets: Predominantly flat desert terrain with a coastline on the Persian Gulf.
Faces extreme summer heat and water scarcity, relying heavily on desalination.

sections.heading: 📜 History & Major Turning Points
bullets: Historically a trading and pearling port on the Persian Gulf.
Became independent from British protection in 1961; invaded by Iraq in 1990, triggering the Gulf War and liberation in 1991.

sections.heading: 🏛️ Major Political & Constitutional Changes
bullets: 1961 independence from Britain.
The 1962 Constitution established a hybrid system combining a hereditary emirate with an elected National Assembly, one of the more participatory systems in the Gulf.

sections.heading: 🏅 Sports, Arts & Global Recognition
bullets: Football is the most popular sport regionally.
Traditional dhow shipbuilding and pearl-diving heritage reflect its Gulf maritime history.

sections.heading: 🌐 International Organizations & Important Memberships
bullets: Founding member of OPEC and the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC).
Member of the UN and the Arab League; the 1990-91 Gulf War was fought over its liberation from Iraqi occupation.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Kuwait is a constitutional emirate at the head of the Persian Gulf, known for the Gulf region's oldest elected parliament and its role in the 1990-91 Gulf War.
keyFacts: Capital: Kuwait City. Currency: Kuwaiti Dinar (among the world's highest-valued currencies).
Constitutional emirate ruled by the Al Sabah family; has the Gulf's oldest elected National Assembly.
Invaded by Iraq in 1990; liberated by a US-led coalition in 1991 (Gulf War).
commonConfusion: Kuwait's 1990-91 Gulf War refers to Iraq's invasion and subsequent liberation — not to be confused with the later 2003 Iraq War.

highYieldFacts: Kuwait: constitutional emirate, capital Kuwait City, Al Sabah ruling family.
Gulf region's oldest elected National Assembly; founding OPEC member.
India-Kuwait: major crude oil supplier to India, large Indian expatriate workforce.
commonTraps: Confusing the 1990-91 Gulf War (Iraq's invasion of Kuwait) with the 2003 Iraq War.
Assuming all Gulf monarchies lack elected legislatures — Kuwait's National Assembly is a notable exception.
mustRemember: Kuwait: constitutional emirate with Gulf's oldest parliament, 1990-91 Gulf War history, key India oil/labour partner.
